statement: Numbers are written in rows. Row 1 is 1. Row 2 is 2, 3. Row 3 is 4, 5, 6. Each new row has one more number than the row before, and the counting continues. What is the first number in row 10?

choices.misconception: I thought each row starts with its own row number, because row 2 starts with 2.
I found the first number of row 9 instead of row 10.
I found how many numbers come before row 10 and gave that, forgetting to add 1.
I found the last number in row 10 instead of the first.

hints: Look at the last number in each row.
The last number in a row equals how many numbers have been written so far, which is 1 + 2 + 3 + ... up to that row. The first number of the next row is one more.
Rows 1 to 9 hold 1 + 2 + ... + 9 = 45 numbers, so row 9 ends with 45.

solutions.reliable: Row n has n numbers, so rows 1 to 9 together hold 1 + 2 + ... + 9 = 45 numbers. That means row 9 ends with 45, and row 10 starts with the next number, 46. Check with the start: row 3 starts at 1 + 2 + 1 = 4, as shown. The transferable idea: in a table that fills row by row, the last entry of a row counts everything written so far, so add up the row lengths.
solutions.elegant: Pair the row lengths: 1 + 9, 2 + 8, 3 + 7, 4 + 6 are four tens, plus 5 makes 45, so row 10 begins at 46.

whyOnTest: Table patterns test whether you can find a position by counting everything that comes before it.
